clue.text: Scottish shellfish very quietly in earth make love?

indicators.note: one thing set in another means the musical letters go inside the soil word

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth
pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft
to do is to make or perform
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A seafood lover asks whether a Scottish clam buried silently in the sand ever gets amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: CLA(PP)Y then DO + O. The question mark flags the jokey idea of a shellfish making love.
explanation.definitionFit: A clappydoo is a Scots dialect name for a large mussel, so it is a Scottish shellfish.

clue.text: Legume I fed to children repeatedly

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes into them, so the letter is put inside

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for child or children, given twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent spoon-feeds peas or beans to the children again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Chich is an old name for the chickpea, which is a legume.

clue.text: German going for Germany in capital part of fuselage

indicators.note: one thing going in place of another means a swap of letters

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for German
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
the British capital

explanation.surface: A German national moves to a capital city in place of a German resident.
explanation.walkthrough: In LONDON the D is replaced by GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A longeron is a main lengthwise structural member of an aircraft's body, so it is part of a fuselage.

clue.text: Spenser's equal trembles to be cast off by one such?

indicators.note: casting something off throws it away, so these letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: one such equal of Spenser: a fellow great Elizabethan poet
to tremble is to shake

explanation.surface: A nervous poet trembles at the thought of being rejected by one of Spenser's peers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One such' points to Shakespeare, a poet to rank with Spenser; take SHAKES off and PEARE remains. Spenser wrote PEARE for peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peare is Spenser's spelling of peer, a person of equal standing.

clue.text: Once in position, plays out time

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been disturbed and need resetting

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A theatre note that, once settled in place, the plays run out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word: Spenser's past participle of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Yplast is an old form meaning placed, so describes something once put in position.

clue.text: Drive forward, light saying you can? (Cobber slow on the uptake)

parts.note: Dr is the street abbreviation for Drive
on as in moving on, forward
a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: Driving instructions about pressing on when the lights say you may, with an aside about a dim Aussie mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobber is Australian slang for a friend, flagging an Australian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drongo is Australian slang for a fool or dimwit, a mate who is slow to understand.

clue.text: What's fed to animal like a cow, endlessly chewed?

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is chopped off
chewed food is mashed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word cow with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Asking what cattle feed on, since it gets chewed the way a cow chews the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcake is compressed seed residue after oil extraction, used as livestock feed.

clue.text: Gap left, oddly, foot short as housing for circular base timber (11, two words)

indicators.note: a house holds something within it, so one part wraps around another
behaving oddly means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
falling short of something means it is missing, so one letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for foot, and it is removed
round means circular

explanation.surface: A builder notes a gap left at an odd angle, a foot too short, beneath a round structure.
explanation.walkthrough: GAP LEFT loses F, the remaining letters become G-PLATE, and ROUND goes inside after the G. 'Oddly' looks like a take-the-odd-letters instruction, but the odd letters of 'Gap left' lead nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground plate is the lowest horizontal timber of a framed building, the sill on which the frame stands.

clue.text: Romancer raising the bar

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it from bottom to top, so it reads upwards

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A storyteller of romance sets a higher standard, raising the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Romancer here means someone who invents fanciful stories, not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To romance is to tell exaggerated or invented tales, so a romancer is a teller of untruths.

clue.text: Townships on north-eastern estate

parts.note: demes were townships of ancient Attica
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A description of some townships on the north-eastern side of a large estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held and worked by its owner, a manor estate.

clue.text: Those little clasps wherein shaft joins head

indicators.note: what is clasped is held tight inside, so the word sits within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Some tiny fasteners where a rod meets a top piece, as on a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf club is the hidden context: shaft and head.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosel is the socket of a golf club head into which the shaft fits.

clue.text: GI's so ill he's in a bad way — it's a form of dysentery

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: An American soldier is very sick, and it turns out to be dysentery.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Shigellosis is bacillary dysentery, the bowel infection caused by Shigella bacteria.

clue.text: Strolling pier, taking in the breeze? That's plain

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside
strolling means wandering about, so the letters move freely

parts.note: taken as written
a breeze is a movement of air

explanation.surface: Walking along the seaside pier and enjoying the breeze is a simple pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective meaning simple, but it is a noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide, treeless grassland, a plain of North America.

clue.text: Independent uhlan, out of order? Line to be drawn

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent

indicators.note: things out of order are not in their proper sequence, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: a uhlan is a lancer; the word is used as written

explanation.surface: An unruly cavalry lancer misbehaves, and someone must draw the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line to be drawn' looks like a figure of speech for a limit, but it is a rope hauled in on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaul is a rope on a boat used to haul in a sail or spar.

clue.text: Clay? See mixture of that and sand

indicators.note: the word is used for its spoken sound, which matches the name of a letter

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced the same way
loam is soil made of clay and sand mixed

explanation.surface: A potter is told to look at clay, then at a blend of clay and sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' refers back to clay, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloam is a dialect word for earthenware or clay, especially in Cornwall and Devon.

clue.text: What nail bar offers, crazy old operation

parts.note: manic means frenzied, crazy
ure is an archaic word for use, practice or operation

explanation.surface: A nail salon offers a wild, old-fashioned procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is cosmetic care of the hands and nails, the service a nail bar sells.

clue.text: Philosopher in male set

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: A thinker belongs to an all-male group.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was the German idealist philosopher known for his dialectic.

clue.text: Such as Goliath, tumbling to a sling? Lo, ——, perhaps

indicators.note: tumbling things fall over and over, landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
these letters are already printed in the clue, so they are taken away

explanation.surface: Goliath and his kind falling to David's sling, as in the Bible: behold, the mighty fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank completes 'Lo, ——' to make an anagram of 'to a sling'; take away the printed LO and the rest fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the Philistine giant, so such as he are giants.

clue.text: Part of sponge I cut in experiment

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: a trial is an experiment
taken as written
ax is the US spelling of axe, to cut

explanation.surface: A scientist cuts a piece of sponge during a laboratory test.
explanation.definitionFit: A triaxial is a sponge spicule with three axes, so part of a sponge's skeleton.

clue.text: Journo following constant rule, to whom one's indebted

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the newspaper worker is placed second, behind the other pieces

parts.note: c is the scientific symbol for a constant such as the speed of light
R is an abbreviation for rule
an editor is a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist who sticks to fixed principles turns out to be someone you owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the journo after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a person or body to whom money is owed.

clue.text: Chief on board retrained usher

parts.note: Ch is an abbreviation for chief

indicators.note: retraining reshapes something, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior executive on the company board is retrained as a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chobdar is an Indian attendant or mace-bearer who ushers visitors in.

clue.text: Jock's following the sun, having mixed deli round the Med e.g.

indicators.note: going round something encloses it
mixed things are stirred together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Mediterranean is a sea

explanation.surface: A Scot chasing sunshine visits a Mediterranean deli with mixed food.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is slang for a Scot, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deiseal is a Scots word for sunwise, moving clockwise in the direction of the sun's course.

clue.text: Typically American, squandering a pile with pep

indicators.note: squandering scatters something wastefully, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An energetic big spender blowing a fortune is a classic American type.
explanation.walkthrough: As American as apple pie is the idiom behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie used as an adjective means wholesomely, quintessentially American, from the idiom.

clue.text: Gym precedes work on Latin and English subjects

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym
op is short for opus, a work
L is the abbreviation for Latin
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A school timetable: gym first, then lessons in Latin and English subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subjects' looks like school courses, but it means citizens of a state.
explanation.definitionFit: The subjects of a ruler are its people, the citizens who owe allegiance.

clue.text: Indulge, putting money in stocks and shares

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside

parts.note: securities are known collectively as paper
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Spoil yourself by investing your cash in the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to indulge someone with excessive comfort and attention.

clue.text: Net user is so like fish being played?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: connected to the internet
second meaning: on the line, hooked by an angler

explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' suggests fishing nets, but it is the internet; the fish is the one on an angler's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browsing the internet is online, and a hooked fish being reeled is on a line.

clue.text: Whom the Irish respect on account of verse (lines penned)

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so these letters are enclosed by others

parts.note: o/a is the commercial abbreviation for on account (of)
L for line, doubled for the plural
v is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: The Irish revere someone for their poetry, a few lines of written verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollav was a learned man or master poet in ancient Ireland, held in great respect.

clue.text: Master giving second in class merit

indicators.note: the second in a word means its second letter only

parts.note: the second letter of class
to merit is to earn

explanation.surface: A teacher awards a merit to the pupil coming second in the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a schoolmaster, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to learn it thoroughly.

clue.text: Migratory thrush, very weird

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for very
eery is a variant spelling of eerie, weird

explanation.surface: A wandering songbird is described as most peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The veery is a North American thrush that migrates south for the winter.

clue.text: Bearing flowers, Jack accepts bereavement well!

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

parts.note: bo is US slang for a pal, as Jack is a familiar name for a man
a bereavement is the loss of someone
my! is an exclamation of surprise, like well!

explanation.surface: A man bravely takes a death in his stride, while flowers surround the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: B(LOSS)O then MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossomy means full of blossom, covered in flowers.

clue.text: Scene with this? Form of mesa clone maybe

definitions.text: Scene with this? Form of mesa clone maybe

indicators.note: a form of something is a different shape of it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
these letters are taken away from the mixture

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what landscape feature goes with a scene, a copy of a mesa perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: SCENE plus the answer is an anagram of 'mesa clone'; the whole clue also describes the answer, a hill much like a mesa.
explanation.definitionFit: A loma is a broad-topped hill or ridge in the US Southwest, a landform similar to a mesa.

clue.text: Former religious rite from Egypt originally, dividing bread

indicators.note: something dividing another splits it, sitting inside it

parts.note: bread and dosh are both slang for money

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: An ancient ritual from Egypt involving breaking bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like food in a ritual, but it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The doseh was an Egyptian dervish ceremony in which the sheikh rode over prostrate devotees, now abolished.

clue.text: Murphy causing gossip round Ireland's capital

indicators.note: going round something encloses it

parts.note: to prate is to gossip or chatter

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the first letter of Ireland

explanation.surface: A man named Murphy stirs up chatter all around Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato, from its association with Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Pratie is an Irish word for potato, which is also called a murphy.

clue.text: Warm stroll round heart of aviary

indicators.note: going round something encloses it

parts.note: to amble is to stroll

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters are used

parts.note: the middle two letters of aviary

explanation.surface: A pleasant walk through the middle of a bird house on a warm day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm' looks like the weather, but it describes a friendly manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm, friendly person is amiable: good-natured and likeable.

clue.text: Driver's first source of unwelcome advice in car, cheerless

indicators.note: the first of a word means its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of driver

parts.words: source of unwelcome advice in car
parts.note: the back seat, home of the back-seat driver

explanation.surface: A motorist's first gloomy experience is unwanted advice from a passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: A back-seat driver offers unwanted tips from the rear of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning gloomy or cheerless.

clue.text: Leaders in nasty lust eye girl askance — thus?

definitions.text: Leaders in nasty lust eye girl askance — thus?

indicators.note: askance means skewed or awry, so the letters are set crooked
leaders are the front runners, so only initial letters are used

parts.note: the first letters of nasty and lust
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men with nasty lust ogle a girl sideways, and the clue asks if that is how they look.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the answer: eyeing a girl askance with lust.
explanation.definitionFit: To look leeringly is to look with a sly, lustful sidelong glance, as described.
